warnings.warning: The Gaussian exponent uses A^{-1} while the following norm is written sqrt(x^T A x) and A is called the covariance matrix. The motivating geometry therefore switches the roles of covariance and precision; future work must define one matrix convention consistently.

Unconstrained pointwise weighted linear extrapolation can yield negative cell values and a field whose total mass is not one. A probability output requires a constrained representation or explicit clipping and renormalization with error checks.

The displayed Euclidean centroid objective sums ||x-x_n||^2 over i, so the summand does not vary with i. Context and the subsequent road objective show that x_i was intended; preserve the source typo as a warning and use x_i in future derivations.

The adapted score is singular at d(x_jk,x_i)=0 and d(x_jk,x_i)=2B unless an exclusion, floor, or limiting convention is imposed. Future implementations must state and test the numerical regularization.

global_organization_chain: Open with two distinct police decisions and a shared location-time evidence base.
Construct one road metric as the common representation before either target model.
Branch into a time-evolving next-crime field and a road-adapted residence field.
Expose a failed naive circle fit, then replace it before using its radius downstream.
Apply the same branch order to two historical cases so evidence remains comparable.
Let the weaker Atlanta next-crime result generate concrete model extensions.
Close with conditional performance boundaries and an executive summary that restates applicability gates before recommendations.

main_argument_chains.claim: A common road metric can make both prediction branches sensitive to automobile accessibility.
support_steps: Map entrances/exits and highway sections to a weighted graph.
Combine Manhattan local connectors with Dijkstra highway paths.
Use the minimum highway-assisted or direct route.
Pass the same distance into kernel, center, and residence-score formulas.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Both hotspot layers can be interpreted under one declared transport representation, while remaining distinct target variables.

main_argument_chains.claim: A time-varying road-kernel field can prioritize possible next-crime locations from earlier incidents.
support_steps: Adapt a normalized KDE to road distance.
Increase bandwidth with incident age to encode recency.
Build historical density snapshots using only incidents available at each time.
Extrapolate each grid-cell trend by weighted least squares.
Inspect one final-event holdout in each case.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The resulting field supplies a relative patrol/search priority, not an absolute event probability or universally validated forecast.

main_argument_chains.claim: A road-metric center and buffer-zone score can prioritize candidate residences.
support_steps: Orient the reader with centrography and competing effort/avoidance mechanisms.
Demonstrate instability of the naive radial circle fit.
Define a squared-road-distance center and mean radius.
Set B=r/2 and adapt Rossmo's score to road distance.
Overlay known residences in both cases.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The residence layer gives an ordered investigation starting point while retaining its heuristic parameter and in-sample evidence boundaries.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper organizes evidence from theory through paired cases to bounded operational advice.
support_steps: The introduction announces theory/implementation before applications.
Both case studies repeat map, next-event, residence, and assessment moves.
The Atlanta miss motivates victim-opportunity and tuning extensions.
The conclusion compares conditions rather than merely repeating outputs.
The executive summary states applicability conditions, two outputs, and complementary use.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: A future modeling paper can imitate the architecture without copying the criminal-case content or treating weaknesses as the primary organizing principle.
